mainTopic: Whether a husband counts as one of the 'people' (בריות) when his wife vows not to benefit from people, and which gifts for the poor she may still use.
overview: The גמרא continues with a woman who vowed not to benefit from 'people' (בריות). Earlier, רב נחמן had said that a husband is not counted among 'people.' רבא challenges him from a משנה about a woman who says 'I am removed from the Jews.' There the husband nullifies only his own part, which suggests he was included in her vow. רב נחמן answers that this case is different: other men are already forbidden to her, so she must have meant her husband. The גמרא then turns to the next line of our משנה, which lets her use לקט, שכחה and פאה. It notes that the משנה leaves out מעשר עני, even though a ברייתא includes it. רב יוסף answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and the משנה follows the רבנן. His source is a משנה where רבי אליעזר says one need not even name the מעשר עני of דמאי. The גמרא explains on the next amud how this ruling connects to her vow.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the case of 'I am removed from the Jews'
steps.stepSummary: רבא questions רב נחמן's rule that a husband is not included in 'people.' He quotes a משנה where the husband nullifies only his own part of a vow that forbids her to 'the Jews.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: Is a husband really not included in 'people'? But we learned in a משנה: If a woman says 'I am removed from the Jews,' her husband nullifies his part. She may be intimate with him, but she stays removed from all other Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's rule by quoting a משנה. In that משנה, the husband seems to be included in his wife's vow about 'the Jews.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the quoted משנה, the husband nullifies only 'his part,' and the rest of the vow stays in force. That suggests the vow covered him to begin with, as one of the Jews. רבא is setting up a contradiction, and he spells it out fully in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: People, the general public
'I am removed from the Jews': a vow forbidding intimacy with her to all Jews
He nullifies his part: only the part of the vow that affects him
She is intimate with him

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
And is a husband not included in 'people'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב נחמן's rule that a wife's vow against 'people' doesn't cover her husband.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.notes: She means that being intimate with her is forbidden to every Jewish man.

phrases.english: and she may be intimate with him,
and she remains removed from the Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's earlier rule, which came before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that a husband is not included in 'people' (בריות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה treats the husband as part of a vow against 'the Jews.' He nullifies only his own share, so he must have been included.

steps.title: Spelling out the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: If the husband were not included, the vow would only hurt her, making it a vow of affliction (נדרי עינוי נפש). Then he could nullify it completely and forever, not just his own part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a husband is not included in 'people,' then these are vows of affliction, and he should be able to nullify the vow for her forever!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the משנה is a problem for רב נחמן. If the husband were not part of the vow, the משנה's ruling would make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the husband were outside the vow. Then it would simply be her harming herself, a נדר of עינוי נפש. A husband can cancel such a vow fully and permanently. But the משנה says only 'his part' is nullified, and she stays forbidden to everyone else, even after a divorce. That only works if he was included in the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say
Vows of affliction: vows that cause the woman suffering, which a husband may nullify
Forever, permanently

phrases.english: a husband is not included in 'people,'
and he should nullify it for her forever!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בַּעַל לָאו בִּכְלַל בְּרִיּוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's challenge by explaining why the quoted משנה contradicts רב נחמן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that the husband is outside 'people'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the husband were excluded, the vow would be pure affliction and fully cancellable. The משנה's partial nullification shows he was included.

steps.title: רב נחמן: that case is different because she clearly meant her husband
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that normally a husband is not included. In 'removed from the Jews,' though, she must have meant him, because only he was permitted to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can say to you: Here it is different. It is clear that she meant to forbid herself from something that was permitted to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his rule. He says the 'Jews' case is a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married woman is already forbidden to every other man. A vow forbidding herself to 'the Jews' would add nothing unless it included her husband, the one man permitted to her. So here the wording clearly includes him. In a general vow against 'people,' the husband is still left out.

keyTerms.meaning: I can say to you: introduces a defense
Here it is different
The matter is clear, the situation proves it
Something permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule stands: a husband is generally not counted among 'people.' In the vow 'removed from the Jews,' he is included only because she must have meant the one man who was permitted to her.

phrases.english: that she is forbidding herself from something permitted.
phrases.notes: Other men are already off-limits to a married woman, so the only 'permitted' one she could mean is her husband.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the husband was included in 'Jews,' he must also be included in 'people.'
steps.terutzMaskana: He is included in 'Jews' only because that vow makes sense only if it covers him. In the general term 'people,' he is not included.

steps.title: The משנה lists לקט, שכחה and פאה, but not מעשר עני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: she may still benefit from לקט, שכחה and פאה. It points out that מעשר עני is missing from the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may benefit from לקט, שכחה and פאה. And it does not teach 'and from מעשר עני.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and makes an observation about what it leaves out. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though she vowed off benefit from people, she may take these gifts for the poor. The reason is that they are taken without needing someone to hand them over as a personal favor. The גמרא notices that מעשר עני is not on the list. Pointing out this gap prepares a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest, left for the poor
Forgotten sheaves, left for the poor
The corner of the field, left for the poor
Poor man's tithe
And it does not teach

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה is forbidding מעשר עני. It just doesn't mention it, and the גמרא is about to ask whether that silence means anything.

phrases.english: from gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and pe'ah.
And it does not teach 'and from poor man's tithe.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who vowed against benefit from people may still use לקט, שכחה and פאה. The משנה does not mention מעשר עני.

steps.title: A ברייתא does include מעשר עני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's silence by citing a ברייתא that adds מעשר עני to the permitted list.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'and from מעשר עני'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a ברייתא that does allow מעשר עני. It asks why our משנה left it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה and the ברייתא seem to disagree about whether she may use מעשר עני. If both sources follow the same view, why would one list it and the other leave it out? The next step answers this contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the observation in step 4 by contrasting it with a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's omission of מעשר עני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly permits מעשר עני, so why does our משנה leave it out?

steps.title: The two sources follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers the contradiction from step 5. The ברייתא, which includes מעשר עני, follows רבי אליעזר. The משנה, which leaves it out, follows the רבנן. He proves that רבי אליעזר is lenient about מעשר עני from a משנה: you do not even have to name the מעשר עני of דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a problem. This source (the ברייתא) follows רבי אליעזר, and that source (the משנה) follows the רבנן. As we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says, a person does not need to designate by name the poor man's tithe of דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא by saying they reflect two different opinions among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the ברייתא includes מעשר עני and the משנה does not. רב יוסף says there is no real contradiction, because each source follows a different תנא. His source is that רבי אליעזר treats מעשר עני of דמאי lightly, since it need not even be named, while the רבנן disagree. The גמרא explains on the next amud how this connects to her vow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The opening words of an answer that removes a contradiction.
This one... that one... Used to give each of two sources its own setting or opinion.
The Sages, the majority opinion that disagrees with a single named תנא.
Produce bought from someone who may not have taken off its tithes, so it is doubtful whether it was tithed.
To designate by name, meaning to declare which portion is the tithe.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which source goes with which opinion. The ברייתא, which includes מעשר עני, is רבי אליעזר. The משנה, which leaves it out, is the רבנן.

phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא from step 5, which does include מעשר עני.

phrases.english: and that one follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is our משנה, which leaves מעשר עני out.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
the poor man's tithe of doubtfully tithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5 between the ברייתא and the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה and the ברייתא follow the same view, so the missing מעשר עני looked like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who is lenient about מעשר עני of דמאי. The משנה follows the רבנן, who disagree, so it does not list מעשר עני.
